correctness.rationale: The finite Hermitian hypercube Hamiltonian has d+1 distinct Walsh eigenvalues. On each eigenspace the two sink projections have rank one at spectral ends, rank two in the interior iff sink distance is between one and d-1, and rank one everywhere for antipodal sinks. Summing ranks gives d+1 or 2d. Every bright eigenvalue of H-iK/2 has negative imaginary part because zero loss implies being in the orthogonal dark eigenspaces, proving eventual absorption equals normalized bright dimension. All 20 finite Krylov rank checks passed.

value.rationale: The problem of optimizing placement of a second irreversible detector on the hypercube is physically motivated and entirely classified, rather than a hand-picked parametric slice. Maximal separation unexpectedly produces no gain, while all remaining geometries are optimizers with an explicit sharp improvement independent of sink strengths. The exact averaged finite-graph transport invariant supplies a useful baseline for studies including disorder/dephasing.
